'''Steven D. Gaines''' is an American marine biologist based in California whose research focuses on fisheries, marine reserves, and marine ecology and conservation.

== Education ==
Gaines received his bachelor's degree in biology from [[University of California, Irvine]], before attending [[Oregon State University]] for his PhD.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Steve Gaines |url=https://bren.ucsb.edu/people/steve-gaines |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=UC Santa Barbara - Bren School of Environmental Science & Management |language=en |archive-date=May 18, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260518121847/https://bren.ucsb.edu/people/steve-gaines |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Bevan Series 2008—Steve Gaines |url=https://depts.washington.edu/donbevan/2008/speakers/gaines.html |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=depts.washington.edu}}</ref> He received his PhD in 1983 under the guidance of [[Jane Lubchenco]] and [[Bruce A. Menge|Bruce Menge]].<ref name=":1" /> His dissertation focused on consumer resource interactions in both Oregon and Panama.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Challenge Bot Detection // ScholarsArchive@OSU |url=https://ir.library.oregonstate.edu/challenge?dest=%2Fconcern%2Fgraduate_thesis_or_dissertations%2F5x21tj209%3Flocale%3Den |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=ir.library.oregonstate.edu |archive-date=December 5, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251205044619/https://ir.library.oregonstate.edu/challenge?dest=%2Fconcern%2Fgraduate_thesis_or_dissertations%2F5x21tj209%3Flocale%3Den |url-status=live }}</ref>

Gaines then moved to [[Stanford University]], where he was a postdoctoral scholar in the lab of [[Joan Roughgarden]] until 1987.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Joan Roughgarden |url=https://web.stanford.edu/~rough/Roughgarden-CV-20200715.html |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=web.stanford.edu |language=EN |archive-date=January 24, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250124175833/https://web.stanford.edu/~rough/Roughgarden-CV-20200715.html |url-status=live }}</ref> His research at Stanford focused on the importance of interspecific interactions and larval delivery in intertidal areas.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gaines |first1=Steven |last2=Brown |first2=Stephen |last3=Roughgarden |first3=Jonathan |date=1985 |title=Spatial Variation in Larval Concentrations as a Cause of Spatial Variation in Settlement for the Barnacle, Balanus glandula |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/4217726 |journal=Oecologia |volume=67 |issue=2 |pages=267–272 |doi=10.1007/BF00384297 |jstor=4217726 |pmid=28311322 |bibcode=1985Oecol..67..267G |issn=0029-8549}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Roughgarden |first1=Jonathan |last2=Gaines |first2=Steven |last3=Possingham |first3=Hugh |date=September 16, 1988 |title=Recruitment Dynamics in Complex Life Cycles |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.11538249 |journal=Science |volume=241 |issue=4872 |pages=1460–1466 |doi=10.1126/science.11538249 |pmid=11538249 |bibcode=1988Sci...241.1460R |archive-date=January 30, 2025 |access-date=July 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250130121506/https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.11538249 |url-status=live}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
Gaines joined the [[Brown University]] faculty in 1987, working there until 1994. He then started a faculty position at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara|University of California Santa Barbara]].<ref name=":1" /> In 1997 he became the director of UCSB's Marine Science Institute.<ref name=":1" /> In 2010, he was appointed as the Dean of the [[UC Santa Barbara Bren School of Environmental Science and Management|Bren School of Environmental Science and Management]] at UCSB, and later was also a strategic advisor for the emLab at UCSB.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steve Gaines {{!}} emLab |url=https://emlab.ucsb.edu/about/our-team/steve-gaines |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=emlab.ucsb.edu |archive-date=December 12, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251212063358/https://emlab.ucsb.edu/about/our-team/steve-gaines |url-status=live }}</ref> Before these positions, he also served as the Acting Vice Chancellor for Research and the Acting Dean of Science at UCSB.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our Team |url=https://resourceslegacyfund.org/our-team/ |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=Resources Legacy fund |language=en-US |archive-date=August 13, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250813121546/https://resourceslegacyfund.org/our-team/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":1" /> He retired from roles as Dean and Distinguished Professor in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bren School of Environmental Science and Management Dean Steve Gaines {{!}} Office of the Chancellor |url=https://chancellor.ucsb.edu/memos/2025-07-09-bren-school-environmental-science-and-management-dean-steve-gaines |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=chancellor.ucsb.edu |archive-date=March 6, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260306181235/https://chancellor.ucsb.edu/memos/2025-07-09-bren-school-environmental-science-and-management-dean-steve-gaines |url-status=live }}</ref>

In 2009, Gaines, along with many other marine ecologists, started the [[Partnership for Interdisciplinary Studies of Coastal Oceans]] with a $17.7 million grant,<ref>{{Cite web |date=August 3, 2009 |title=Major $17 million grant to fund ocean research {{!}} Newsroom {{!}} Oregon State University |url=https://news.oregonstate.edu/news/major-17-million-grant-fund-ocean-research |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=news.oregonstate.edu |language=en}}</ref> studying the long-term health of nearshore environments on the US west coast. Gaines also co-founded the Santa Barbara Coastal [[Long Term Ecological Research Network|LTER]] project, focusing on kelp forests.<ref name=":1" /> He has published numerous articles on marine ecology and climate change, including the impacts of temperature on larval settlement and dispersal,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=O'Connor |first1=Mary I. |last2=Bruno |first2=John F. |last3=Gaines === Marine reserves ===
In 2003, Gaines was awarded a [[Pew Fellowship in the Arts|Pew Fellowship]], allowing him to help implement the [[Marine Life Protection Act]] in California. This act established a statewide coastal marine network in the state.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Steven D. Gaines, Ph.D. |url=http://pew.org/2bDJ6Ui |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=pew.org |language=en}}</ref><ref name="auto">{{Cite web |title=Using Outcomes from Marine Protected Area Implementation to Infer Potential Socioeconomic Consequences of Offshore Energy Development to Commercial Fisheries {{!}} UCSB Marine Science Institute === Fisheries management ===
Gaines' research includes market based reforms to make fisheries management more sustainable,<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Steve Gaines {{!}} Latin American Fisheries Fellowship Program |url=https://www.laff.bren.ucsb.edu/laff-network/steve-gaines |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=www.laff.bren.ucsb.edu |archive-date=December 17, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20251217064304/https://www.laff.bren.ucsb.edu/laff-network/steve-gaines |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Future of Food: The Rise of the Sea {{!}} Steve Gaines |url=https://tedxsantabarbara.com/talk/steve-gaines/ |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=tedxsantabarbara.com |archive-date=April 20, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260420024852/https://tedxsantabarbara.com/talk/steve-gaines/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Costello |first1=Christopher |last2=Gaines |first2=Steven D. |last3=Lynham |first3=John |date=September 19, 2008 |title=Can Catch Shares Prevent Fisheries Collapse? |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1159478 |journal=Science |language=en |volume=321 |issue=5896 |pages=1678–1681 |doi=10.1126/science.1159478 |pmid=18801999 |bibcode=2008Sci...321.1678C |issn=0036-8075 |archive-date=June 29, 2025 |access-date=July 23, 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250629110946/https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.1159478 |url-status=live }}</ref> including the role of [[aquaculture]].<ref name=":3" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Castillo |first1=Liliana Sierra |last2=Ferguson Irlanda |first2=Caroline E. |last3=Aceves-Bueno |first3=Erendira |last4=Froehlich |first4=Halley E. |last5=Mancilla |first5=Cristina |last6=Rivera |first6=Antonella |last7=Gaines |first7=Steven D. |date=October 1, 2025 |title=Aquaculture isn't always the answer: rethinking blue transitions through justice and community experience |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0959378025000834 |journal=Global Environmental Change |volume=94 |article-number=103046 |doi=10.1016/j.gloenvcha.2025.103046 |bibcode=2025GEC....9403046C |issn=0959-3780}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zhao |first1=Kangshun |last2=Gaines |first2=Steven D. |last3=García Molinos |first3=Jorge |last4=Du |first4=Juan |last5=Wang |first5=Hongxia |last6=Zhang |first6=Min |last7=Xu |first7=Jun |date=February 1, 2026 |title=Aquaculture coupled with trade is sustaining growth and improving stability in global aquatic food supply |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0044848625013468 |journal=Aquaculture |volume=613 |article-number=743460 |doi=10.1016/j.aquaculture.2025.743460 |bibcode=2026Aquac.61343460Z |issn=0044-8486}}</ref> He has also focused much of his career on understanding the link between marine protected areas and fisheries health and sustainability. Most of this work focuses on the importance of strong networks of many small marine protected areas that can increase fisheries yield.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gaines |first1=Steven D. |last2=White |first2=Crow |last3=Carr |first3=Mark H. |last4=Palumbi |first4=Stephen R. |date=October 26, 2010 |title=Designing marine reserve networks for both conservation and fisheries management |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |volume=107 |issue=43 |pages=18286–18293 |doi=10.1073/pnas.0906473107 |doi-access=free |pmc=2972919 |pmid=20200311}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> He, along with Chris Costello, founded the Sustainable Fisheries Group in 2006, which later provided the foundation for emLab. His work on fisheries has expanded to include the importance of improving fisheries management to offset the negative impacts of climate change.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Gaines |first1=Steven D. |last2=Costello |first2=Christopher |last3=Owashi |first3=Brandon |last4=Mangin |first4=Tracey |last5=Bone |first5=Jennifer |last6=Molinos |first6=Jorge García |last7=Burden |first7=Merrick |last8=Dennis |first8=Heather |last9=Halpern |first9=Benjamin S. |last10=Kappel |first10=Carrie V. |last11=Kleisner |first11=Kristin M. |last12=Ovando |first12=Daniel |date=August 29, 2018 |title=Improved fisheries management could offset many negative effects of climate change |journal=Science Advances |volume=4 |issue=8 |article-number=eaao1378 |doi=10.1126/sciadv.aao1378 |pmc=6114984 |pmid=30167455 |bibcode=2018SciA....4.1378G }}</ref> This work was also named a top scientific contribution by the journal [[Nature (journal)|Nature]] in 2008.<ref name=":4"/>

== Awards and honors ==
Gaines has served on editorial and advisory boards for many organizations, including Ecology and [[Ecological Monographs]] and the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref name=":0" /> In 2009 he was named an [[American Association for the Advancement of Science|American Association for the Advancement of Science fellow]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=UCSB |date=December 17, 2009 |title=Seven UCSB Faculty Members Named AAAS Fellows |url=https://www.noozhawk.com/121709_seven_ucsb_faculty_members_named_aaas_fellows/ |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=Noozhawk |language=en-US |archive-date=December 3, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231203010412/https://www.noozhawk.com/121709_seven_ucsb_faculty_members_named_aaas_fellows/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Elected Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=American Association for the Advancement of Science (AAAS) |language=en |archive-date=October 7, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181007145732/https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing |url-status=live }}</ref><ref name=":4" /> That same year, he received the inaugural Marc J. Hershman Excellence in Mentoring Award from the [[Joint Ocean Commission Initiative]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Staff |first=Indy |date=July 21, 2009 |title=More Than a Teacher |url=https://www.independent.com/2009/07/21/more-than-teacher/ |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=The Santa Barbara Independent |language=en-US |archive-date=February 19, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250219081337/https://www.independent.com/2009/07/21/more-than-teacher/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=UCSB |date=July 20, 2009 |title=UCSB Professor Wins National Mentoring Award |url=https://www.noozhawk.com/072009_ucsb_professor_wins_national_mentoring_award/ |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=Noozhawk |language=en-US}}</ref> He was awarded a [[Peter Benchley Ocean Award]] for Excellence in Science in 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Excellence in Science |url=https://www.peterbenchleyoceanawards.org/excellence-in-science |access-date=July 23, 2026 |website=peter benchley awards |language=en-US |archive-date=August 27, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250827032627/https://www.peterbenchleyoceanawards.org/excellence-in-science |url-status=live }}</ref> He has published over 300 scientific articles and 4 books in his career.<ref name=":4" />
